root.name: Indian Defense: Paleface Attack, Blackmar-Diemer Gambit Deferred

overview: Against 1.d4 Nf6 White plays 2.f3 and 3.e4 after ...d5, a Blackmar-Diemer Gambit deferred. If Black takes with 3...dxe4 4.Nc3 reaches a BDG-type game, while Black can strike with the Kraus-Muhlherr counter-gambit 3...e5 4.dxe5 Nxe4. White builds a broad centre and attacks quickly, but Black's counterplay is easy.

white_ideas.idea: Build a centre with e4, Nc3 and attack on the kingside

black_ideas.idea: Take on e4 and consolidate, or strike with ...e5
Use extra pawn and ...c5 or ...e5 breaks

gambit.notes: 3.e4 dxe4 gives a pawn that Black can keep.

soundness.notes: Strong players consider the f3/e4 plans dubious.

approach.notes: Rare and played mostly for surprise.

level.notes: Dubious so not a good first choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: Kraus-Muhlherr Counter Gambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. f3 d5 3. e4 e5 4. dxe5 Nxe4
sublines_that_differ.how: Black strikes back in the centre.

character.reason: Gambit play with an open centre and exposed kings.

gambit.reason: 3.e4 offers a pawn that Black can keep.

soundness.reason: Black can consolidate or counter without risk.

structure.reason: Central pawn exchanges and open lines follow.

plans.reason: White plays for development and an attack for the pawn.
